summary: The complete legal domain has only 298 (n, k) pairs, n is at most 12, and even the largest unrestricted result contains only 377 strings, leaving no honest runtime scaling range for an output-generating algorithm.

workload_bound.source_constraint: n is an integer between 1 and 12 inclusive

replacement_checks.evidence: The remotely accepted and app-local implementations visit only prefixes that respect the cost and adjacency guards; each visited prefix extends with zeros to a returned string, so at most O(n * R) states are visited, while the recursion and path are bounded by n.

The certificate regression checks both stored source forms for all 298 legal (n, k) pairs against independent enumeration of all 2^n binary strings, including duplicate detection; authored cases cover n = 1 and n = 12, zero and maximum budgets, index-zero cost, adjacency pruning, cost pruning, and unordered output.
